text: Dressed in my fine new clothes, I moved into an expensive private hotel in Hanover Square, and everything there was on credit. <break time="0.8s" /> Harriss eating house became famous because I had eaten there, and Harris was so grateful that he forced loans on me. <break time="0.8s" /> Everywhere I went, people wanted to serve the strange millionaire who carried a million pound note in his vest pocket. <break time="0.8s" /> The newspapers called me the vest pocket million pounder, and I became one of the best known men in London. <break time="0.8s" /> Punch, the famous comic magazine, even printed a cartoon of me in rags, bargaining with a guard for the Tower of London. <break time="0.8s" /> Still, I kept a careful record of my debts, for I hoped to pay them all back from my future salary. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon the American minister, who had been a school friend of my fathers, invited me to a dinner party at his house. <break time="0.8s" /> There I met a lovely English girl named Portia Langham, and I fell in love with her in two minutes. <break time="0.8s" /> It was at that very dinner that an old friend from San Francisco, Lloyd Hastings, suddenly walked in. <break time="0.8s" /> Later that evening, I told Portia the whole story from the start, and she laughed until she could hardly breathe.
